# 01_cover

Welcome. Today we're presenting findings from Google Cloud's landmark report documenting 1,001 real-world generative AI use cases from leading organizations worldwide. What started as 101 entries at Cloud Next 2024 has grown tenfold in just 18 months — spanning 11 industries and 6 distinct agent types. This isn't a vision document. It's a production deployment ledger.

[Pause]

The scale tells a story: enterprise gen AI has moved from experimentation to mainstream adoption faster than most predicted.

Key points: ① 1,001 verified production use cases ② 11 industry verticals, 6 agent types ③ 10× growth in 18 months signals exponential phase
Duration: 1.5 minutes

---

# 02_growth_trajectory

[Transition] Let me set the context by tracing the growth trajectory that brought us here.

In April 2024, Google Cloud published its first list — 101 use cases — at Cloud Next. By mid-2024, that number had roughly quadrupled. By early 2025, it crossed 600. And as of October 2025, the list stands at 1,001 use cases, with 400 new entries added in the latest update alone.

[Data] The authors themselves note this still only scratches the surface.

[Pause] The inflection point is clear: we are in the early exponential phase of enterprise gen AI deployment.

Key points: ① 10× growth from 101 to 1,001 in 18 months ② 400 new entries in the October 2025 update alone ③ Still early — pace is accelerating
Duration: 2 minutes
Flex: [If time is tight, skip the mid-2024 and early-2025 milestones and go directly to the 10× headline]

---

# 03_taxonomy_matrix

[Transition] To make sense of 1,001 use cases, you need a framework. Google Cloud organizes them along two dimensions: industry vertical and agent type.

Eleven industries — from Automotive and Financial Services to Public Sector and Telecommunications. Six agent types — Customer, Employee, Creative, Code, Data, and Security. This taxonomy gives you a structured way to identify where your organization fits and where the highest-impact opportunities lie.

[Scan Room] Notice the highlighted row for Automotive and Logistics — that's where we'll drill in next.

[Pause] The density indicators show that Customer and Employee agents dominate across nearly every industry, while Creative and Code agents are concentrated in specific sectors but growing fast.

Key points: ① 11×6 matrix provides structured adoption framework ② Customer and Employee agents are densest ③ Automotive highlighted for deep-dive
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 04_automotive_deep_dive

[Transition] Let me walk you through the Automotive and Logistics vertical as a representative deep-dive — it provides one of the richest cross-sections of agent types.

Starting with Customer agents: Mercedes-Benz has deployed the MBUX Virtual Assistant powered by Gemini for natural in-car conversations. LUXGEN, a Taiwan EV maker, reduced customer service workload by 30 percent with a Vertex AI chatbot on LINE. GM's OnStar improved intent recognition. VW's myVW app lets drivers query owner's manuals using multimodal capabilities. UPS Capital uses ML to score delivery confidence. And PODS generated over 6,000 unique ad headlines across 299 New York City neighborhoods in just 29 hours.

[Data] Thirty percent workload reduction and 6,000 headlines in 29 hours — these are not pilot metrics.

For Employee agents: Toyota's factory AI platform saved over 10,000 man-hours per year. Uber uses AI agents to summarize customer service communications. Rivian, Geotab, and Routematic all use Gemini for Workspace across research, onboarding, and legal review.

And in the Code agent category, Renault's Ampere division uses Gemini Code Assist for EV software development.

Key points: ① Customer agents: 6 companies, in-car to curbside ② Employee agents: 5 companies, measurable efficiency ③ Code agents: Renault/Ampere developer productivity
Duration: 3 minutes
Flex: [If time is tight, cover only Mercedes-Benz, LUXGEN, Toyota, and Renault — these have the strongest metrics]

---

# 05_roi_highlights

[Transition] The deep-dive was qualitative. Now let me surface the most compelling quantified outcomes across all industries.

[Benchmark] Four numbers to remember. First, Mercari — Japan's largest online marketplace — anticipates 500 percent ROI while reducing employee workloads by 20 percent through AI-powered customer service. Second, LUXGEN cut customer service workload by 30 percent with a Vertex AI chatbot. Third, Toyota saved over 10,000 man-hours per year with their factory AI platform. And fourth, PODS generated 6,000-plus unique headlines across all 299 NYC neighborhoods in just 29 hours.

[Pause] I want to emphasize: these are production results, not pilots. These organizations are live and measuring.

[Data] Five hundred percent ROI is extraordinary for any technology investment, let alone one deployed within months.

Key points: ① 500% ROI — Mercari ② 30% workload reduction — LUXGEN ③ 10,000+ hours/year saved — Toyota ④ 6,000+ headlines in 29 hours — PODS
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 06_cross_industry_patterns

[Transition] Looking across all 1,001 use cases, three dominant patterns emerge.

Pattern one: Conversational Customer Agents are the most visible entry point. From Mercedes-Benz's in-car assistant to GM OnStar to LUXGEN's chatbot to Mercari's 500-percent-ROI service — every industry is deploying AI-powered virtual assistants to handle customer queries and reduce human agent workloads.

Pattern two: Employee Productivity Agents are the broadest category. Uber, Rivian, Geotab — these companies use Gemini for Workspace to summarize documents, accelerate research, draft content, review legal documents, and filter data across departments from HR to engineering. The breadth is what's notable here.

[Pause] Pattern three — and this is the one to watch — Creative at Scale is the fastest-growing frontier. Virgin Voyages creates thousands of hyper-personalized video ads using Veo. Figma generates brand-approved assets in seconds. PODS adapts billboards in real time. Gen AI is moving from text into multimodal creative production at enterprise scale.

Key points: ① Customer agents = most common entry point ② Employee agents = broadest applicability ③ Creative agents = fastest-growing frontier
Duration: 2.5 minutes
Flex: [If time is tight, focus on pattern three — the Creative at Scale trend — as it's the most forward-looking]

---

# 07_strategic_takeaways

[Transition] Let me close with five actionable takeaways for your organization.

First, gen AI is production-ready across all 11 major industries. This is not a future vision — 1,001 deployments are live right now.

Second, Customer and Employee agents are the most common entry points. Start here. These are the lowest-risk, highest-impact deployments with the most proven ROI.

Third, measurable ROI is achievable within months — not years. Five hundred percent ROI, 30 percent workload reduction, 10,000-plus hours saved. These are real numbers from real companies.

Fourth, Creative and Code agents are emerging fast. The transition from text-only to multimodal — video, imagery, adaptive content — is the next frontier.

[Pause]

And fifth: the pace is accelerating. Four hundred new entries in the latest update alone. Early movers build institutional knowledge and operational advantages that compound over time.

[Scan Room] The strategic question is not whether to deploy gen AI — it's how fast you can move.

Key points: ① Production-ready across all industries ② Start with Customer and Employee agents ③ ROI within months is achievable ④ Multimodal is the next frontier ⑤ Early movers gain compounding advantages
Duration: 3 minutes
Flex: [If time is tight, cover takeaways 1, 2, and 5 only — these are the most actionable for decision-makers]
